newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up in active trading on Friday on overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 23,860 yuan ($2,877) per tonne, rising 240 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 24,000 and hit a low of 23,830.
June rose 190 to 23,500, July 200 to 23,700, August 220 to 23,810 and October 260 to 23,860. The November contract, which was traded for the first time, closed at 23,750.
Combined volume rose sharply to 72,480 tonnes from 35,830.
Copper opened higher but profit-taking pushed the prices down for most of the session, traders said.
Traders said the LME gains boosted the confidence of long position holders but rises met strong resistance.
"LME gains were responsible for today's rises but copper met strong resistance at the 24,000 yuan level," one trader said.
"Many cautious investors liquidates their long positions at high levels today," he said.
Physical prices are around 23,400 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area.
Traders said it would be difficult for Shanghai futures to breach the key 24,00-yuan level in the short term judging from Friday's trading.
"Shanghai copper will not easily breach the key resistance unless the LME continues to rise sharply in the next few days," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended mixed. June rose 50 to 15,500, July 180 to 15,850 and August fell 50 to 15,850.
Combined volume fell to 1,610 tonnes from 1,650.
